---
title: "Git guard"
description: "Refuse new remote branches and pull requests on configured machines with ttr git guard, keeping fleet work on the direct-to-main flow."
updatedAt: "2026-11-16"
---

## Why this exists

Fleet machines publish `tutur3u/platform` and `upskii/platform` work directly to
`main`: review locally, rebase onto `origin/main`, commit as the configured
identity with a DCO sign-off, push fast-forward only, then run `bun git-sync`.
Pull requests and new remote branches from fleet machines are not part of that
flow. `ttr git guard` enforces it on each opted-in machine. Pushes are refused
before Git makes any network write, and PR creation is refused before `gh`
contacts GitHub.

## What it enforces

The guard applies only to pushes whose remote resolves to a guarded repository
(default: `tutur3u/platform`, `upskii/platform`). It matches on the last two
path segments of the remote URL, so https, ssh and scp-style remotes all match.
Credentials in a URL are never logged.

| Push | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `main` / `production`, fast-forward | allowed |
| `main` / `production`, non-fast-forward, create or delete | refused; no override |
| new branch (anything else) | refused; overridable |
| existing non-main branch | refused by default (`existingBranches: "allow"` to permit); overridable |
| existing `release-please--branches--*` | allowed; creating one is refused |
| branch matching `allowBranches` | allowed |
| deleting a non-protected branch, any tag | allowed and logged |
| other refs (`refs/notes/*`, …) | refused; overridable |

The ancestry check runs locally (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`). A stale clone
that lacks the remote commit is refused until you fetch and rebase.

The gh guard refuses these on guarded repositories:

- `gh pr create` (and its alias `gh pr new`)
- `gh api` POSTs to `repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls`
- `gh api graphql` with `createPullRequest`
- `gh stack submit`

The repository comes from `-R/--repo`, `GH_REPO`, the REST path, or the
working directory's remotes. A GraphQL creation whose repository cannot be
resolved is refused. Every other `gh` command passes straight to the real `gh`
without starting Bun.

### Release flows that keep working

- release-please, Dependabot and the `release-*-package` workflows push from
  GitHub Actions, so client hooks never see them.
- `bun git-sync` pushes `main` and `production` as fast-forwards.
- `bun git-release-please` merges locally into `main`, then pushes `main` as a
  fast-forward.
- `scripts/tuturuuu-bot-token.js` (task-branch push plus `gh pr create`) is
  refused on guarded machines by design. A real exception uses a one-shot
  override.

## Install and operate

```bash
ttr git guard install --shell zsh          # or bash / none
ttr git guard status                       # add --json for receipts
ttr git guard log --limit 20
```

`install` writes `~/.tuturuuu/git-guard/` (honours `TTR_GIT_GUARD_HOME`):

- `config.json`: opt-in config (`enabled`, `machine`, `repos`,
  `ffOnlyBranches`, `existingOnlyPrefixes`, `allowBranches`,
  `existingBranches`).
- `hooks/`: managed dispatchers. The global `core.hooksPath` points here.
  Each dispatcher chains to the hook the repository would otherwise run: the
  repo's recorded `ttr-guard.chainHooksPath` (for example `.githooks`), the
  previous global hooksPath, or `.git/hooks`. `.githooks/pre-push`, Git LFS and
  similar hooks keep working.
- `bin/gh`: the gh shim. A managed shell block puts it first on `PATH`.
  A gh alias cannot do this, because aliases cannot shadow built-in commands.
- `log.jsonl`: every refusal, guarded allow, override creation and
  consumption, install and uninstall.

A clone with a local `core.hooksPath` (this repository sets `.githooks` on
`bun install`) would bypass a global hooksPath. Two mechanisms close that gap:

- `install --repo <path>` repoints such clones and records the previous value.
- `scripts/install-git-hooks.js` keeps a clone on the guard's directory whenever
  `git config --global ttr-guard.hooksPath` names an installed guard.

`ttr git guard status` flags any listed clone that still bypasses the guard.

`ttr upgrade` and `ttr upgrade activate` refresh the hook and shim through the
new release. `ttr git guard uninstall` restores the previous hooksPath values and
shell files, and keeps the log.

## Exceptions

There is no environment-variable bypass. A real exception (release-please,
Dependabot, a USER-approved stack) uses an explicit override:

```bash
ttr git guard allow-once --kind push --repo tutur3u/platform \
  --ref <branch> --reason "<why>" --approved-by <who>
ttr git guard allow-once --kind pr --repo tutur3u/platform \
  --reason "<why>" --approved-by <who>
```

Overrides:

- need a reason and an approver
- expire after 15 minutes by default (`--ttl-minutes`, at most 120)
- are consumed by an atomic rename, so exactly one push or PR creation uses each
  one
- are logged both when created and when consumed

Protected-branch rewrites and deletions cannot be overridden.

## Limits and server-side backstop

Client hooks are advisory: `git push --no-verify` skips them, and the GitHub MCP
server talks to the API directly instead of through `gh`. On guarded machines,
agent configurations should deny MCP pull-request creation tools. The durable
backstop is a GitHub repository ruleset that restricts branch creation, with
bypass for the release-please, Dependabot and Actions identities. That ruleset
is a repository-administration decision and is not applied by the CLI.

## Rollout check

On each machine, after `ttr upgrade` and `ttr git guard install`:

1. `git push origin HEAD:guard-probe/<machine>` from a guarded clone is refused,
   and no remote branch appears.
2. `gh pr create --head guard-probe/<machine>` in the same clone is refused.
3. `ttr git guard status --json` shows the hook current, global hooksPath active,
   the gh guard active, and both refusals in `lastRefusals`.

Regression coverage lives in `packages/sdk/src/cli/git-guard-*.test.ts` and
`scripts/install-git-hooks.test.js`.
